title: Legacy Digital Twin: Interview Question Bank

field_notes.answer_mode: voice | text | either (suggested only; always allow both)
field_notes.emotionally_heavy: true = pace it: max one per day, never two days in a row, never at bedtime by default, offer skip/snooze, follow with a light prompt next session
field_notes.teaches: what the answer trains in the twin: memory, voice, values, advice, humor, decision_style, emotion, relationships, identity, tastes, routine, worldview, comfort, family_history, boundaries
field_notes.per_child: true = ask once per child; substitute [child name] and store answer tagged with that child_id
field_notes.placeholders: [child name] = substitute per child; [partner name] = substitute the co-parent/partner's name, or rephrase if not applicable
field_notes.revisit: none | yearly (re-ask ~12 months later and keep both answers, dated) | per_milestone_and_yearly (re-record as the child ages)
field_notes.use_in_twin: retrieval = memory store for RAG; persona_prompt = summarise into persona/system prompt; guardrail = hard rules for the twin; voice_style = phrasing exemplars; scheduled_message = deliver at milestone, verbatim, as a recording, never regenerated
field_notes.est_minutes: rough time to answer, including follow-ups

categories.label: Tastes: music, food, places, books, movies
Opinions on money, work, success & health
Phrasing & voice: how he says things
What he wants his kids to know about him
How he wants to be remembered

items.prompt: Close your eyes for a second and walk me through the front door of the house you remember most from being a kid. What do you see, hear and smell?
follow_ups: Which room did you spend the most time in, and why?
Is there one object from that house you wish you still had?
What did the house sound like at night?

items.prompt: What was your neighborhood like? Who lived next door, and where did the kids go to play?
follow_ups: Was there a place you weren't supposed to go but did anyway?
Who was the neighbor everyone talked about?

items.prompt: Describe your mom the way you'd describe her to someone who never got to meet her.
follow_ups: What's a phrase she said so often you can still hear it?
What did she do with her hands when she was thinking or worried?
What did she teach you without ever meaning to?

items.prompt: Describe your dad the way you'd describe him to someone who never got to meet him.
follow_ups: What did he do when he was proud of you, and did he say it out loud?
What's something about him you only understood once you became a dad?
What did he smell like? Coffee, sawdust, aftershave?

items.prompt: What did you need from your parents as a kid that you didn't always get? How has that shaped the kind of father you try to be?
follow_ups: When did you first notice that gap?
Have you made peace with it? What did that take?

items.prompt: If you had brothers or sisters, or cousins who felt like them, tell me about them as kids. Who was the troublemaker, who was the peacemaker, and which one were you?
follow_ups: What's the best prank or fight you remember?
Who did you go to when you were in trouble?

items.prompt: What kind of student were you? Tell me about a teacher you loved and one you couldn't stand.
follow_ups: What subject made time disappear for you?
Did anyone at school see something in you before you saw it yourself?

items.prompt: What did a perfect Saturday look like when you were ten?
follow_ups: What toys, games or shows were you obsessed with?
Who were you with?

items.prompt: Who was your best friend growing up? How did you meet, and what did you two get up to?
follow_ups: Do you still talk? What happened?
What did that friendship teach you about being a friend?

items.prompt: What scared you as a kid? How did you deal with it, and who helped?
follow_ups: Is any of that fear still with you in some form?
What would you tell little you about it now?

items.prompt: Tell me about a time you got in real trouble as a kid. What did you do and what happened next?
follow_ups: Did you deserve it?
How did your parents handle it, and would you handle it the same way?

items.prompt: Was money tight, comfortable, or something nobody talked about in your house growing up? How did you know?
follow_ups: What's a moment you first realised what things cost?
How did that shape how you handle money now?

items.prompt: What were the unspoken rules in your family? The things everybody just knew you did or didn't do.
follow_ups: Which of those rules have you kept?
Which ones did you deliberately break with your own kids?

items.prompt: Was there a hard season in your childhood, an illness, a move, a divorce, a loss, that changed the feel of home? Tell me about it only as far as you want to.
follow_ups: Who held things together?
What did you understand then, and what do you understand now?

items.prompt: What's the first thing you remember being really proud of yourself for?
follow_ups: Who did you want to show?
Do you still feel a little of that pride when you think about it?

items.prompt: What did dinner look like in your house growing up? Who cooked, where did everyone sit, and what was the meal you hoped for?
follow_ups: Was there a dish you hated but had to eat?
Is there a recipe from that kitchen that should be passed down?

items.prompt: Start at the very beginning: where and when were you born, and what's the story you've been told about the day you arrived?
follow_ups: Who told you that story?
What do you know about what the world was like that year?

items.prompt: What's your very earliest memory? Describe it in as much detail as you can, even if it's blurry.
follow_ups: How old do you think you were?
Why do you think that moment stuck?

items.prompt: Who were you at thirteen? What did you care about, what did you wear, what did you worry about?
follow_ups: What would thirteen-year-old you think of you now?
What music was playing in your room?

items.prompt: Tell me about your teenage years: the friends, the trouble, the first job, the first car, the first time you felt grown up.
follow_ups: What's a night from those years you'll never forget?
What did you think your life would look like by now?

items.prompt: Who was your first crush or first love, and what was that like?
follow_ups: How did it end?
What did you learn about yourself?

items.prompt: What were your twenties like? Where did you live, what did you do for money, and what did you do for fun?
follow_ups: What's the worst apartment you ever lived in?
What were you searching for in that decade?

items.prompt: What was the biggest gamble you took in your twenties? How did it turn out?
follow_ups: Would you take it again?
Who tried to talk you out of it?

items.prompt: What was the loneliest or most lost you felt as a young adult? How did you find your way back?
follow_ups: What, or who, was the turning point?
What would you say to one of the kids if they felt that way?

items.prompt: Tell me about your thirties. What was taking most of your energy, and what was giving you energy back?
follow_ups: What did you start taking more seriously?
What did you stop caring about?

items.prompt: What was it like becoming a dad, in that decade of your life? What changed first, outside and inside?
follow_ups: What surprised you the most?
What did you lose, and what did you gain?

items.prompt: What does your forties feel like, or what did it feel like? What do you know now that you didn't at thirty?
follow_ups: What are you still figuring out?
What's become simpler?

items.prompt: Looking at the decades still ahead of you, what do you hope each one holds? Tell me about the version of you at sixty, seventy, eighty.
follow_ups: What do you want to be doing on an ordinary Tuesday at seventy?
What are you afraid of about getting older?

items.prompt: What's going on in your life right now, this week? Just a snapshot for the record.
follow_ups: What's on your mind most days lately?
What's something small that made you happy this week?

items.prompt: If your life were a book, what would the chapters be called so far? Give me the titles and a sentence for each.
follow_ups: Which chapter was the hardest to live through?
What do you want the next chapter to be called?

items.prompt: List every place you've lived, in order, and give me one sentence about each.
follow_ups: Which one felt most like home?
Which one would you go back to?

items.prompt: What big world events happened during your life that you remember exactly where you were for? Tell me about one.
follow_ups: How did it change the way you saw the world?
How did the people around you react?

items.prompt: Tell me about a moment where your life could have gone one of two ways. Which way did you go, and why?
follow_ups: What do you think the other version of you is doing?
Did you know at the time it was a big moment?

items.prompt: What's the best decision you ever made? Walk me through how you made it.
follow_ups: Was it a gut call or did you think it through?
What did it cost you?

items.prompt: What's a decision you'd unmake if you could? What happened, and what do you understand about it now?
follow_ups: What made it feel right at the time?
How have you lived with it?

items.prompt: Who walked into your life at exactly the right time? Tell me about that meeting.
follow_ups: Did they know how much they mattered?
Where are they now?

items.prompt: Tell me about a loss that divided your life into before and after.
follow_ups: What did you do in the first days after?
What helped, and what did people say that didn't help?
How do you carry it now?

items.prompt: Was there a moment you suddenly saw yourself clearly, maybe not in a flattering way, and decided to change?
follow_ups: What did you actually change?
Did it stick?

items.prompt: Where in your life did luck play a bigger part than you usually admit?
follow_ups: And where did hard work get less credit than it deserved?
How do you think about luck when you talk to the kids?

items.prompt: When were you the bravest you've ever been?
follow_ups: Did anyone see it?
What gave you the nerve?

items.prompt: Has your view of faith, meaning or the big questions ever shifted dramatically? What triggered it?
follow_ups: What did you lose and what did you find?
How did the people around you react?

items.prompt: Has your health or the health of someone close to you ever forced a turning point? What happened, and what did it change in how you live?
follow_ups: What did you promise yourself then?
Have you kept it?

items.prompt: What's a tiny, almost random moment that ended up changing everything, like a wrong turn, a conversation, a flyer on a wall?
follow_ups: Do you believe in coincidences?
Who else was there?

items.prompt: What was your very first job? How much did it pay and what did you learn from it?
follow_ups: Worst boss or best boss from back then?
What's a story from that job you still tell?

items.prompt: How did you end up doing the work you do now? Tell me the real story, including the detours.
follow_ups: Was there a moment you almost quit?
Who opened a door for you?

items.prompt: Explain what you do to one of the kids at age ten. Then explain it the way you'd explain it to a colleague.
follow_ups: What part of it do you love so much you'd do it for free?
What part of it drains you?

items.prompt: What does doing your work really well look like? What do the best people in your field do that others don't?
follow_ups: How did you learn that?
What's a piece of craft knowledge you'd hate to see lost?

items.prompt: What tools, methods or habits do you swear by in your work, and why?
follow_ups: What's something everyone in your field does that you think is wrong?
What would you teach an apprentice on day one?

items.prompt: Tell me about the piece of work you're proudest of. What went into it?
follow_ups: What almost went wrong?
Who should get credit that didn't?

items.prompt: Tell me about a professional failure that really stung. What happened, and how did you get back up?
follow_ups: What did you say to yourself at the time?
What would you say to the kids if the same thing happened to them?

items.prompt: Who taught you the most about work? Mentors, bosses, coworkers, even people you didn't like.
follow_ups: What exactly did they teach you?
Did you ever tell them?

items.prompt: Have you ever been asked to do something at work that didn't sit right with you? What did you do?
follow_ups: Where's your line?
Did it cost you anything?

items.prompt: If you've built things, apps, tools, a team, anything, what made you want to build them? What does building feel like when it's going well?
follow_ups: What did you build that nobody knows about?
What are you building right now?

items.prompt: Has work ever cost you time with the family that you wish you had back? Tell me honestly.
follow_ups: What did you change because of it?
What would you tell the kids about that balance?

items.prompt: What should one of the kids know before they take their first real job?
follow_ups: How do you know when it's time to leave a job?
How do you ask for a raise?

items.prompt: How do you think work will change in the kids' lifetimes, and what skills do you hope they hold onto no matter what?
follow_ups: What do you hope never gets automated away?
What are you excited about?

items.prompt: If you had to boil down what you believe about how to live into five rules, what would they be?
follow_ups: Which one is hardest for you to live by?
Where did each one come from?

items.prompt: What does being a good person actually mean to you, day to day, not in theory?
follow_ups: Who's the best person you've ever known, by that standard?
When do you fall short?

items.prompt: How do you think about honesty? Is there ever a time a lie is the right thing?
follow_ups: Tell me about a time you told a hard truth.
Tell me about a time you wish you had.

items.prompt: Tell me about a small act of kindness someone did for you that you've never forgotten.
follow_ups: Have you paid it forward?
Why do you think it stuck with you?

items.prompt: What do you believe about God, the universe, or whatever's bigger than us? It's fine if the answer is complicated or 'I don't know'.
follow_ups: How has that changed over your life?
What would you want the kids to know about how you got there?
What do you hope they believe, if anything, and what would you never want to force on them?

items.prompt: What do you think happens after we die? And how do you feel about that?
follow_ups: Does it comfort you or scare you?
How would you want the kids to talk about it?

items.prompt: What makes a life meaningful? How do you know when yours feels meaningful?
follow_ups: When did life feel least meaningful, and what brought it back?
Is meaning found or made?

items.prompt: What's an injustice in the world that really gets under your skin? What do you think people should do about it?
follow_ups: Have you ever acted on it?
What do you want the kids to do when they see unfairness?

items.prompt: How do you deal with people whose beliefs are very different from yours?
follow_ups: Have you ever changed your mind because of someone like that?
Where do you draw the line?

items.prompt: What's something you believed strongly once and later changed your mind about? What changed it?
follow_ups: How did it feel to admit it?
What do you believe now that you suspect you'll change your mind about?

items.prompt: What are you most grateful for right now? Go past the obvious.
follow_ups: Who haven't you thanked that you should?
What's something small you're grateful for every day?

items.prompt: Where do you feel most at peace or most in awe? Describe the place and the feeling.
follow_ups: When were you last there?
Would you want the kids to go there to think of you?

items.prompt: What do you believe about forgiveness? Is there anything you haven't forgiven, or haven't been forgiven for?
follow_ups: What would it take?
What do you want the kids to know about forgiving you?

items.prompt: How often do you think about your own death, and how does thinking about it change how you live?
follow_ups: What made you want to build this twin?
What are you hoping it gives the kids?

items.prompt: How do you want the twin to handle politics and hot-button topics? Share your general outlook and tell me how much of it you want the twin to say out loud.
follow_ups: Which views are firm for you, and which are you unsure about?
What do you want the kids to know about how you formed your opinions, not just what they are?

items.prompt: Are there any practices, prayer, meditation, journaling, long walks, that keep you grounded?
follow_ups: When did you start?
What happens when you skip it?

items.prompt: What are you proudest of in your whole life? Not your résumé, the thing that actually makes your chest feel full.
follow_ups: Who helped make it happen?
Does anyone know how much it means to you?

items.prompt: What's something you're proud of that nobody would ever guess?
follow_ups: Why have you kept it quiet?
Would you want the kids to know?

items.prompt: What's a moment one of the kids made you prouder than you could say? Tell me exactly what happened.
follow_ups: Did you tell them?
What do you hope they remember about that day?

items.prompt: What's your biggest regret? Take your time.
follow_ups: What would you need to do, or have done, to let it go?
What did it teach you?
What do you want the kids to take from it so they don't repeat it?

items.prompt: Is there someone you owe an apology to? What would you say to them?
follow_ups: Is there still time to say it?
What's stopping you?

items.prompt: What's a regret you used to have that you've made peace with? How?
follow_ups: What finally shifted?
Do you ever slip back?

items.prompt: What's a lesson you had to learn more than once?
follow_ups: Why do you think it took so long?
How would you teach it to the kids faster?

items.prompt: What do you know now that you wish someone had told you at eighteen?
follow_ups: Would you have listened?
Who did try to tell you?

items.prompt: What's the best piece of advice you ever got, and who gave it to you?
follow_ups: And the worst?
Did you follow the good one right away?

items.prompt: What's something most people believe that you think is wrong?
follow_ups: How did you come to see it differently?
Is there a chance you're the one who's wrong?

items.prompt: Tell me about a mistake that turned out to be one of the best things that ever happened to you.
follow_ups: Did you realise it right away?
Who laughed about it with you?

items.prompt: If you could relive one day of your life exactly as it was, which day would it be? And if you could redo one day differently, which one?
follow_ups: What would you notice this time?
What would you do differently?

items.prompt: Tell me the story of how you met [partner name], or the great love of your life, from your point of view. What did you notice first?
follow_ups: When did you know?
What did your friends think?

items.prompt: What has your marriage or your longest relationship taught you about love that you didn't know going in?

What's the best thing?

items.prompt: What has been the hardest period in your love life, and how did you get through it, or not?

What would you want the kids to understand about that time?

items.prompt: What do you love most about your partner that the kids might not see?

How do you show them you love them?

items.prompt: How do you know when you love someone? How would you describe that feeling to one of the kids?
follow_ups: How is loving a partner different from loving a kid?
Is love a feeling or a decision?

items.prompt: What's the most romantic thing you've ever done, or tried to do and messed up?
follow_ups: How did it go over?
What would you do differently now?

items.prompt: Tell me about a heartbreak before you met your partner. How did you get over it?
follow_ups: How long did it take?
What helped the most?

items.prompt: Who are your closest friends right now, and what makes each of those friendships work?

What's a friendship you let slip that you miss?

items.prompt: What makes someone a good friend? What makes someone a friend you should let go of?

items.prompt: What should the kids watch out for in a partner? And what should they look for?

items.prompt: What does a healthy fight between two people who love each other look like?
follow_ups: What's a rule you and your partner have for arguing?

items.prompt: Beyond family, what groups or communities have you belonged to, teams, congregations, online groups, neighbors, and what did you get from them?
follow_ups: Which one shaped you most?

follow_ups: What did you feel holding them for the first time?
What was the first thing you said to them?

items.prompt: What did you think being a dad would be like, and how is it actually?
follow_ups: What's harder than you expected?
What's better than you expected?

items.prompt: Describe each of your kids in a paragraph, as they are right now. Who are they? What lights them up?

items.prompt: What's a funny story about each kid when they were little that they've probably forgotten?

items.prompt: What are the little things you do with the kids that are just yours, bedtime routines, car games, inside jokes, special breakfasts?

items.prompt: What skills have you taught the kids or wanted to teach them? Riding a bike, cooking, fixing things, writing code, being kind?

items.prompt: What's it like watching the kids grow up? What do you notice that they don't?

What do you hope you never forget?

items.prompt: What do you want the kids to know about [partner name] from your point of view, things you admire or that make her who she is?

items.prompt: If any of the kids become parents themselves, what would you want them to know going in?
